prompt: Create a high-fidelity desktop web homepage design comp for Plexus, a multilingual white-label operating layer for cross-border B2B programs. Landscape 1536×1024 composition, clearly a responsive website interface—not a poster, brochure, or moodboard. Direction: “The Summit Table,” rooted in multilingual trade-summit agendas, delegate placards, and signed communiqués. The first viewport must prove the product mechanism immediately: structured company profile → organizer-reviewed match → mutual acceptance → confirmed meeting → agreement and follow-up. Use real product wording: “Sharper connections for cross-border business.” Primary action: “White-label with Plexus.” Secondary action: “Join as a business.” Preserve a clearly designated Plexus logo area but do not invent a new logo. Show navigation for How it works, For vendors, For businesses, Pricing, language choices EN / BM / 繁體中文, and Login. Structure: an offset vertical agenda rail at left with numbered journey stages; a large central two-party exchange table showing two company profile placards moving toward a confirmed meeting; concise headline and CTA integrated into the composition rather than a standard split hero; begin the second fold with three crisp operator outcomes. Palette: coal ink #111a17, mineral white #f2f4ef, deep jade #0d6b55, signal coral #f05b3d. Materials: crisp mineral paper, enameled agenda tabs, embossed seal detail. Build depth from bold overlapping flat color fields, not generic floating cards or glass. Typography: modern, narrow, highly legible sans with decisive scale; support multilingual copy. Human-governed, precise, internationally credible, simple enough to extend into an Admin dashboard. No neon glow, no purple, no generic SaaS bento grid, no gradients, no fake customer logos, no testimonials, no unverified statistics, no invented market claims. Include enough of the next section to prove the system governs the full page.
